question: Question linked to image nº16 A 54-year-old black woman with asthenia, drowsiness, paresthesias, gait disorder, and loss of strength and sensation in both lower extremities. The analyzes showed Hb 10.4 g / dL, VCM 107 fL, platelets 110,000 / mm3, leukocytes 5,000 / mm3, neutrophils 1900 / mm3, lymphocytes 2500 / mm3, monocytes 300 / mm3, eosinophils 300 / mm3, reticulocytes 1.0% (normal: 0.5-2), total reticulocytes 5,400 / mm3, haptoglobin 0 g / L (normal 0.3-2 g / L), LDH 1,114 U / L, AST (GOT) 50 U / L, ALT ( GPT) 30 U / L, GGT 16 U / L, alkaline phosphatase 90 U / L, total bilirubin 1.03 mg / dL. Negative Coombs test. The peripheral blood smear is shown in the image. Assessed the clinical and analytical picture, what is the treatment that should be administered to this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "54-year-old black woman with anemia" -> "Hb 10.4 g/dL indicates possible macrocytic anemia" -> "VCM 107 fL suggests macrocytic red blood cells" -> "Symptoms of paresthesias and gait disorder suggest possible vitamin deficiency" -> "Negative Coombs test rules out autoimmune hemolytic anemia" -> "Peripheral blood smear likely shows megaloblastic changes" -> "Parenteral vitamin B12 is indicated for vitamin B12 deficiency" -> 85%

CHAIN: "54-year-old black woman with asthenia and drowsiness" -> "Anemia with Hb 10.4 g/dL and VCM 107 fL" -> "Symptoms of paresthesias and gait disorder" -> "Possible vitamin B12 deficiency due to neurological symptoms" -> "Negative Coombs test suggests non-immune hemolysis" -> "Haptoglobin 0 g/L indicates hemolysis" -> "Parenteral vitamin B12 treatment is appropriate" -> 90%

CHAIN: "54-year-old black woman with macrocytic anemia" -> "Symptoms include paresthesias and gait disorder" -> "Anemia with low reticulocyte count" -> "Negative Coombs test suggests no autoimmune process" -> "Haptoglobin low indicates hemolysis" -> "Peripheral blood smear shows megaloblastic features" -> "Parenteral vitamin B12 is the most likely treatment" -> 80%

CHAIN: "54-year-old black woman with anemia and neurological symptoms" -> "Hb 10.4 g/dL and VCM 107 fL indicate macrocytic anemia" -> "Symptoms of paresthesias and gait disorder suggest vitamin deficiency" -> "Negative Coombs test rules out autoimmune hemolytic anemia" -> "Haptoglobin low indicates hemolysis" -> "Parenteral vitamin B12 is indicated for treatment" -> 75%
analysis: The clinical presentation and laboratory findings suggest a macrocytic anemia with signs of hemolysis (elevated LDH, low haptoglobin) and neurological symptoms, which are indicative of vitamin B12 deficiency. The negative Coombs test rules out autoimmune hemolytic anemia. Given the symptoms and laboratory results, the most appropriate treatment is parenteral vitamin B12, which addresses both the anemia and the neurological manifestations.
